subject: PhysioTech on-prem blueprint: air-gapped site, egress/BGP & NVMe cache
messages:
From: Alicia Moreno <alicia@physiotech.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem deployment kickoff: air-gapped site + egress requirements

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on. We're preparing an air-gapped private deployment at our Austin R&D site and want Redwood to run the inference stack there. Key constraints up front:

- Site will be air-gapped for model download/testing windows (no continuous internet).
- Dual-rack footprint: cross-rack failover required; prefer symmetric capacity.
- GPUs: we'll provision 8x A100-equivalent per rack initially (can be adjusted).
- Storage: central SAN for PVs (encrypted at-rest), plus local NVMe on each node as a high-performance cache/KV for model serving.
- Egress: all outbound traffic must leave through our provider edge via BGP (no NAT through customer LAN).
- Compliance: SOC 2 in scope; KMS integration mandatory.

Attached: physiotech_site_network_diagram.vsdx (network sketch) and a rough SOW.

Can we align on a high-level cluster blueprint and a short checklist for airgap onboarding before the procurement window (we need vendor approvals by 2026-12-08)?

--
Alicia Moreno
CTO, PhysioTech Labs

Jonas — Monday works. Quick answers for sizing:

- Steady-state inference: ~120 requests/sec (burst to 350 RPS for short windows), 95th %ile latency target <= 250ms.
- Model artifacts: ~2TB total initial, expecting growth ~10% month. Need snapshot backups retained 90 days.
- KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault HSM (PKCS#11) for keys and expect Redwood to integrate with our KMS for model keys and disk encryption keys.
- Preferred GPU: 80GB-class (A100-80) with 1 replica per model for canary rollouts.

I've attached PhysioTech_SOW_draft_v1.pdf with procurement timeline. Procurement is pulled in on the cc.

Thanks,
Alicia
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:41:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: PhysioTech onprem blueprint — initial tech assumptions and open questions

Team — summary and items to validate before the customer sync. Quoting Alicia below where relevant.

Summary assumptions (proposed):
- Cluster control plane: 3 control-plane nodes on management VLAN, dedicated management switch, OOB access via jumpbox.
- Node pools:
  * infra/mgmt: 3x m6-standard (ETCD, monitoring, logging collectors)
  * compute-cpu: mixed small scale for online preprocessing
  * compute-gpu: 2 racks x 8 GPUs (A100-80 class) distributed across two node pools for fault isolation; each node pool will have mixed-size nodes to allow bin-packing.
- Storage:
  * PVs: primary persistent volumes served from SAN via iSCSI/FibreChannel (customer-managed). Use CSI driver with volumeAttachment secrets managed through Vault.
  * Local NVMe: use as ephemeral KV cache for model KV and attention caches; mount as ephemeral emptyDir with local PV for workloads that require high IOPS.
  * Backups: velero-style snapshotting to air-gapped object store during allowed windows; snapshots pushed via an approved transfer node.
- Networking:
  * Egress requirement: customer requires BGP peering. Recommend MetalLB in BGP mode for service IPs + a small eBPF-based egress controller to ensure outbound flows exit at the physical provider edge.
  * IP design: avoid NAT hairpins; use explicit route advertisements to their edge AS.
- Security/compliance:
  * KMS integration: Vault PKCS#11 + HSM. Need to validate key rotation windows and whether Redwood will generate model keys or use customer-provided.
  * Audit logs: collect and forward to on-site SIEM via TLS (certs to be provisioned).

Open questions for Alicia/procurement before we finalize blueprint:
1) Preferred CSI driver (CSI-iSCSI or vendor-specific FC) and whether we will manage multipath.
2) Is cross-rack replication required at block layer or will application-level replication suffice?
3) Who will supply BGP ASN and edge peering config? (customer or MSP?)
4) Window schedule for pushing model artifacts into air-gapped site (dates/times).

I'll present this high-level at the sync and capture responses. Please add edits.

- Jonas

Jonas / Aditya — quick security & ops checklist additions before customer meeting: 

- KMS: confirm exact PKCS#11 provider string and HSM endpoints; we must capture the CSR process for certs inside the air-gapped environment.
- Supply chain: require code-signing verification for any runtime images pushed in — provide Sigstore envelope or offline GPG signatures.
- Audit: ensure control-plane RPCs (kubectl exec, port-forward) are logged with session replay enabled for SOC2 evidence.
- Airgap model delivery: require a signed manifest and SHA256 checksums for every artifact; define transfer node with strict firewall rules.
- Egress/BGP: we can support both customer-provided ASN and a managed peer if procurement prefers; need the peering window and contact.

I've attached an internal playbook link (https://drive.redwood.company/drive/physiotech/onprem-templates) with templates for the CSR and offline image checklist. I'll prepare the KMS integration steps and a short runbook for transfer-node ops.

LG,
